To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Infomap algorithm is a promising tool for community detection in directed graphs, that the WalkTrap algorithm achieves the highest accuracy, that the Label Propagation algorithm has an outstanding performance in scalability, and that the Eigenvector algorithm is not a good choice for directed graphs.
WalkTrap, Infomap and Label Propagation are the most accurate and scalable algorithms to detect communities in directed graphs.
the algorithms that are specifically designed to process directed graphs (Infomap and Label Propagation) achieve a good trade-off between accuracy, scalability and computational performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

two main issues: (1) the evaluation of the accuracy and scalability of the algorithms to detect communities in directed graphs; and (2) the application of the algorithms in Web Data Analytics to understand the structure and evolution of Web-based systems.
the development of a community detection algorithm that is accurate, scalable and able to process directed graphs.

the problem of finding communities in directed graphs and, in particular, we focus on the application of community detection algorithms to the problem of Web graph analysis and prediction of its evolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, there is not an algorithm which is always better than others, as the best algorithm to use depends on the specific application and on the characteristics of the input data.
there is no single best algorithm to detect communities in directed graphs.
there is no best community detection algorithm for directed graphs, but that each of the algorithms we tested has some advantages in specific situations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the absence of any a priori information, the best choice is to use WalkTrap; however, if the user is interested in scalability, the best choice would be Label Propagation, while Infomap should be preferred if the user is also interested in accuracy.
community detection algorithms that ignore edge directionality can provide good quality results but, in general, the best accuracy is achieved by algorithms that explicitly consider directed graphs.
, when the graph is directed, the best approach is to use a method designed for directed graphs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, on directed graphs, the best algorithms are not the best in terms of accuracy but the best in terms in terms of trade-offs between computational performance and accuracy.
the choice of the algorithm is a crucial step for the community detection task.
community detection in directed graphs is not a solved problem and that the choice of the best algorithm is highly dependent on the application domain.
